In this key role, you will lead significant and high-profile initiatives related to land use planning and capital projects across the state, acting as the primary wetland liaison to federal, state, local, and tribal partners. 

As a senior planner, you’ll coordinate strategic planning and policy implementation, provide internal leadership across multidisciplinary teams, and supervise a team of wetland specialists. 

Your work will directly support environmental permitting efforts by delivering the wetland science and regulatory support that protect fish and wildlife habitats, align with agency goals, and foster collaboration across a wide network of stakeholders. 


WHAT TO EXPECT -
Among the varied range of responsibilities held within this role, this position: 

Statewide Project Environmental Permit Review and Requirements. 
Assist Senior and Executive Management in identifying new policies and regulations, new direction of existing policies and regulations, and significant initiatives that could most affect liaison to state, local, federal, and other external entities, as well as work areas that would be improved by new policy, new direction, or initiative development.
Determine wetland and mitigation requirements for CAMP-assigned projects. Determine scheduling and budget of project goals and needs. Prepare, submit, and review wetland delineation and mitigation submittal packages, including supporting environmental permit documents. Review projects for environmental and Endangered Species Act impacts. 
Maintain environmental law, regulation, and environmental permit compliance through oversight, facilitation, and compliance with environmental elements of project implementation, including environmental permitting requirements, special evaluations, and Best Management Practices (BMP) usage.
Work within the Mid-Management Team (MMT) or other identified entity to develop and maintain a consistent state-wide approach to new policies, new directions on existing policies, and significant initiatives.
Serve as Liaison and Regulation Policy Lead for projects/issues/processes that are impacted by new or redirected regulation policies or significant initiatives.
Conduct strategic analyses concerning agency or externally developed regulation policies, redirected policies, or significant initiatives.
Communicate and/or present strategic analysis information to the Environmental Permitting Manager for coordination with Senior Management or Executive Management and assist in development of strategic and tactical steps to accomplish agency and partner goals that are consistent with the Agency mission.
Work with the Environmental Permitting Manager, Project teams, Program teams, and supervised staff to implement strategic direction by identifying specific actions and using a continuous strategic approach, such as the utilization of Plan, Do, Check, Adjust (PDCA) methodology, to ensure the Agency is appropriately responsive to changes in the social, political, or biological environment.
As Liaison, assist the Environmental Permitting Manager to actively engage local, state, or federal agencies and other external entities important to the success of the identified strategic direction.
Provide senior-level technical expertise in wetland science and management, including ecology, delineation and rating, regulation, mitigation, enhancement, and restoration.

Supervision.
Provides guidance, direction and information to staff regarding Program/Agency policies, procedures, and directions in a clear and timely manner.
Works with staff to develop strategic approach to accomplishing goals, addressing issues and successfully implementing assignments. Conducts regular (at least monthly) one-on-one sessions with staff to communicate, track, and develop strategies to address issues and accomplish assignments.
In collaboration with staff, develops and provides training for professional staff.
Provides mentoring to staff to promote and support professional development.
Works with individual staff to provide guidance and direction regarding workload control and prioritization.
Provides performance management to staff.
Land Use Planning: Directs, guides, and provides information to staff for successful engagement in land use planning and development.
Major Projects: Directs, guides, and provides information to staff for successful engagement in Major Project activities.

Program Strategic Planning.
Position actively engages to assist Senior and Executive Management in Program or Agency level short-term and long-term strategic planning.
Position works with Environmental Permitting Manager and other Program staff to develop and bring an environmental permitting perspective to Program/Agency strategic planning.
The AEPS, with Environmental Permitting Manager, is responsible for communicating and encouraging support for the strategic direction identified by the Program and/or Agency.


Working Conditions:

Work setting: Duties are performed in an office setting, construction sites, in and around water including swift water, in remote regions with limited to no cell phone coverage, and in areas where hunters may be present. This position may involve working in or near water, including tasks that require navigating, negotiating, and performing duties related to water environments. Climb ladders and work from boats and elevated locations. Fieldwork also requires knowledge of the operation of a GPS, clinometer, and digital camera. Physical capacity to work in remote forested and aquatic environments, conducting fish surveys and other related tasks. These activities can occasionally consist of days in excess of 8 hours, for several days in a row.

Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM. Workload may require additional hours, and the incumbent may be expected to adjust the work schedule to meet business needs.

Travel requirements: Travel will be required throughout the state to attend training, meetings, and conferences. Travel for fieldwork will also be required. Periods of overnight travel may be required, and work hours may exceed the standard 8 am to 5 pm workday. Travel may comprise up to 20%.

Customer Interactions: Agency staff, other government agencies, tribal, private stakeholders, and general public.

Required Qualifications:

Option 1:
A Master's degree or above in physical sciences, natural sciences, environmental sciences, environmental planning, natural resource planning or management, or other closely related fields.
And
Three (3) years of professional experience in environmental science, natural resource planning or management, wetland delineation and mitigation, physical science, natural science, and/or natural resource-related program development.

Option 2:
A Bachelor’s degree in physical sciences, natural sciences, environmental sciences, environmental planning, natural resource planning or management, or other closely related fields.
And
Five (5) years of professional experience in environmental science, natural resource planning or management, wetland delineation and mitigation, physical science, natural science, and/or natural resource-related program development.

Option 3:
An Associate’s degree in physical sciences, natural sciences, environmental sciences, environmental planning, natural resource planning or management, or other closely related fields.
And
Seven (7) years of professional experience in environmental science, natural resource planning or management, wetland delineation and mitigation, physical science, natural science, and/or natural resource-related program development.

For ALL of the above:
Valid driver’s license.
Three (3) years of supervisory experience.


Preferred Qualifications:
In addition to the required qualifications, our ideal applicant will possess some or all the following:
A Professional Wetland Scientists (PWS) certification
Be proficient with the Washington Tool for Online Rating (WATOR) put out by the Washington State Department of Ecology
Utilizing ArcGIS to analyze and map spatial data
Strong leadership experience
Successfully developing and delivering educational content to diverse audiences, demonstrating effective teaching and communication skills.
Building and maintaining productive partnerships with tribal governments, the public, and local, state, and federal agencies to support collaborative environmental initiatives.
Applying knowledge of Pacific Northwest ecological processes to inform habitat assessments, conservation planning, and regulatory reviews.
Interpreting and applying environmental regulations, including the Hydraulic Code, Growth Management Act (GMA), State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA), and Shoreline Management Act (SMA), in support of environmental permitting and land use decisions.
Managing competing priorities and meeting project deadlines through strong organizational and time management skills.
Reviewing and monitoring environmental permits to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, supporting environmentally responsible development and resource protection.
Proven success in delivering clear, concise, and effective verbal and written communications to diverse internal and external audiences.
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build trust, foster collaboration, and maintain positive working relationships across teams and stakeholder groups.
Skilled at translating complex or sensitive topics into accessible language while maintaining a respectful and non-confrontational tone.

Make a difference in fish conservation and fish health statewide. 

In this role, you will lead a team of microbiology professionals, oversee critical laboratory, and provide essential fish health services supporting more than 80 hatchery facilities. 

Your expertise will help identify and respond to viruses, bacteria, parasites, and other microbes affecting fish populations while directly contributing to the health and sustainability of the state’s fish resources.


What to Expect-
Among the varied range of responsibilities held within this role, the Senior Fish Health Microbiologist will,

Plan, supervise, and coordinate all laboratory activities within the WDFW Microbiology Laboratory, including the design and implementation of microbiological investigations:
Plan, assign, prioritize, and evaluate the work of microbiology laboratory staff to ensure timely completion of diagnostic testing, surveillance activities, and research projects. 
Conduct performance evaluations, establish performance expectations, and provide ongoing feedback and corrective action when necessary. 
Lead regular staff meetings to communicate priorities, procedural updates, quality assurance findings, and organizational initiatives. This includes supervising all work of the microbiology staff at all subdisciplines (e.g., virology, bacteriology, microscopy, biochemistry, molecular genetics). 
Ensure laboratory activities meet established biosecurity and agency safety standards. 
Ensure all equipment is functioning to specification, maintains inventory of laboratory supplies, and is responsible for accounts payable database. 
Adapt existing technologies to address emergent problems and conducts quality analysis/control and final review of new protocols. 
Maintain continual surveillance over tests performed to assure adherence to proper technique and necessary standards of accuracy. 

Implement virological, bacteriological, biochemical, molecular genetics, and gross methods to detect pathogens and parasites:
Sample processing, plating, steaking, maintenance of cell culture and cell lines, culture isolation, and the cryopreservation of viral positives and cell lines. 
Conduct microscopy, RNA and DNA extractions, qPCR, PCR, RT-PCR, Sanger and genomic sequencing, viral cytopathic effect (CPE) identification of certifiable aquatic animal pathogens, biochemistry assays (e.g., ELISA), antibiotic sensitivity testing, API testing, necropsies, and maintaining logs.

Inform and consult with fish health professions within and external to WDFW:
Write (or review and validate for staff), and distribute laboratory reports and data to WDFW management, WDFW fish health and hatchery staff, fish health co-managers and co-operators, including tribal, local, state, federal, and international fish health partners.        
 

Working Conditions: 

Work setting, including hazards: 
May encounter exposure to the following:  
Infectious aquatic animal pathogens (viral, bacterial, fungal, and parasitic) and biological specimens during laboratory testing and necropsies.
Biohazardous materials such as blood, tissues, bodily fluids, and contaminated laboratory waste.
Laboratory chemicals and reagents, including stains, preservatives, disinfectants, solvents, acids, bases, and molecular biology reagents.
Cryogenic materials (e.g., liquid nitrogen) and ultra-low temperature freezers during specimen preservation and storage.
Ultraviolet (UV) light, lasers, or other instrumentation used in molecular diagnostics.
Compressed gases used with laboratory equipment.
Noise from laboratory equipment such as centrifuges, biosafety cabinets, freezers, and ventilation systems.
Risk of cuts or punctures from scalpels, needles, broken glass, and other laboratory sharps.
Electrical hazards from laboratory instrumentation and equipment.
Repetitive hand and wrist movements from pipetting, microscope use, and computer work, with prolonged standing or sitting.
Occasional lifting and carrying of laboratory supplies, sample coolers, compressed gas cylinders (using appropriate equipment), or equipment, generally up to 30–50 pounds.
Slips, trips, and falls associated with wet laboratory environments.

Schedule: Work is on-site at the Natural Resource Building in Olympia, Washington. Typically, Monday – Friday, 8:00 A.M. – 4:30 P.M., 40 hours per week. The standard work schedule includes the potential for occasional evening or weekend work as needed. Alternative schedules may be considered based on business needs.

Travel Requirements: Limited - occasionally for meetings and assistance at hatcheries.

Tools and Equipment: Biological safety cabinets, microscopes, PCR/qPCR instrumentation, DNA/RNA extraction and sequencing equipment, ELISA analyzers, cell culture equipment, centrifuges, incubators, autoclaves, ultra-low temperature freezers, liquid nitrogen storage systems, laboratory glassware and necropsy instruments, analytical laboratory equipment, computers, laboratory information management systems (LIMS), laboratory coat or disposable gown, nitrile or latex gloves, safety glasses or chemical splash goggles, face shield, respiratory protection, inverted microscope, confocal microscope, pipettors, centrifuge, scalpels, forceps, homogenizer, biosafety cabinet, ultracold freezers, freezers, refrigerators, incubators, sequencer, endpoint PCR, quantitative PCR, autoclave, dry-heat sterilizer, scale, pH meter, clock, heat block, gel rig, cameras, DI water system, dishwasher, computers, plate-washer, optical density spectrometer multi-well plate reader, automated dispenser.

Customer Interactions: Limited interaction with public. Daily interaction with hatchery and field staff.


Qualifications:

Closely related qualifying experience may be substituted for the required education on a year-by-year basis. 

Required Qualifications: 

A bachelor's degree in science with major study in microbiology, pathobiology, chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, medical technology, or closely allied field. 

*Including at least 20 semester or 30 quarter credit hours in college coursework in microbiology or related fields. 

And the following (experience may be gained concurrently): 
Six (6) years of experience working in microbiology laboratories with demonstrated working knowledge of the following:  
Molecular methods (PCR, sequencing, and protocol development)
Bacteriology, virology, chemistry, parasitology, mycology, immunology
Laboratory terminology, techniques, and equipment including standard analyses, microscopic examinations and histological staining methods used in the identification of microbes
Microbiology research methods and requirements
Report preparation and sources of data on current microbiology research
At least one (1) year of leadership or supervisory duties including conflict resolution, training and development, planning and assigning work and evaluating performance.

Please Note: 
A master’s degree in one (1) of the above fields may be substituted for one (1) year of experience.
A Ph.D. degree in one (1) of the above fields may be substituted for two (2) years of experience.

Knowledge of organization and operation of microbiology laboratories including diagnostic tests and techniques in fields of serology, and microscopy; current microbiology research for salmonids and other finfish; scientific report writing for salmonids and other finfish.

Planning, organizing, directing, coordinating and evaluating work of technical/professional laboratory personnel.
Working cooperatively with personnel of state, local public, and private laboratories to perform research studies.
Writing and establishing standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Working in a biosafety level 2 (BSL) facility or certified laboratory.

Scientific Leadership:
Provide leadership, vision, and direction for science activities in Eastern Washington, ensuring that science activities are focused on high-priority topics with strong management and policy implications. 
Develop a forward-looking Eastern Washington science program encompassing an all-H (Habitat, Harvest, Hatcheries, Hydropower) management framework.

Science-Policy Interface:
Serve as WDFW technical representative on Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) related committees and workgroups designed to evaluate and adaptively manage the direct and indirect effects of hydropower development and operations on fish populations. 
Serve as point person on the development and implementation of scientifically robust monitoring and evaluation programs and other science needs in Eastern Washington associated with implementation of WDFW Anadromous Salmon and Steelhead Hatchery Policy, Hatchery Management Plans, and Hatchery Genetic Management Plans.
Provide a clear and defensible scientific foundation for FERC mitigation decisions, and summarize, interpret, and communicate science needed to meet FERC mitigation requirements.
Summarize, interpret, and communicate science to be used in ongoing litigation over Endangered Species Act Biological Opinions for federal dams in the Columbia River.

Supervision:
Supervise the Hatchery-Wild Interactions (HWI) Unit Leader and Salmon Recovery Science (SRS) Unit Leader and oversee approximately 90 staff within the Fish Science Division. 
The HWI Unit consists of five (5) research teams in Eastern Washington with a primary responsibility for monitoring and evaluation of all WDFW salmon and steelhead hatchery programs in Eastern Washington.
The SRS Unit consists of two (2) research teams in Eastern Washington. The SRS Unit has primary responsibility for the foundational monitoring and evaluation of WDFW fisheries, population status and trends of salmon, steelhead, and bull trout in Eastern Washington.

Administration:
Negotiate and secure contracts, agreements, and programmatic funding to support science needs for conservation, fisheries management, and recovery.
 

Working Conditions: 

Work Setting, including hazards: 

Majority of work is performed in an office setting (90%) with some field work. Field work includes smolt and adult fish trapping operations, Passive Integrated Transponder (PIT) Tag operations, working at hatchery facilities, and conducting stream surveys. 

Hazards include navigating uneven and slippery terrain, slips, and trips. 

This position may involve working in or near water, including tasks that require navigating, negotiating, and performing duties related to water environments.

Schedule: Typically, Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.  40 hours per week with some flexibility. 

Travel Requirements: Frequent travel is required within and outside Washington State.

Customer Relations: Regular interactions with local, state, tribal, and federal agencies as well as Public Utility Districts (PUDs), non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and regional recovery organizations.


Qualifications:

Closely related qualifying experience may be substituted for the required education on a year-by-year basis.  

Required Qualifications:

A Master's degree in fisheries science, biology or zoology or a closely allied field. 

AND all of the following: 
Eight (8) years of professional experience designing and conducting multidisciplinary fish-related research studies. 
Demonstrated professional experience supervising, leading, and coaching employees, including performance management.
Six (6) articles published in peer-reviewed literature, including:   
Four (4) articles for which you are the senior author.
Two (2) additional articles for which you are the senior or secondary author.

Certifications/Licenses:
Valid unrestricted Driver’s License.


Preferred Qualifications:
In addition to the required qualifications, our ideal applicant will possess one or more of the following:
A Ph.D. in fisheries science, biology or zoology or closely allied field.
Experience with analytical tools and statistical modeling used in the management of salmon and steelhead populations, including abundance estimation, life cycle models, and management strategy evaluation.
Knowledge of Columbia Basin fish populations, hydropower operations and mitigation agreements, and recreational and commercial fisheries.
Ability to work directly with tribal co-managers in the Columbia Basin on various topics including monitoring and evaluation, population status and trend, hydropower impacts, predation, and climate change issues.
 

Your application should include the following:
A completed online application showcasing how your qualifications align with the job requirements.
An up-to-date resume. 
A cover letter detailing your interest in the position, your relevant skills and experience, and why you are the ideal candidate.
At least three professional references with current contact information.

TPWD MISSION

To manage and conserve the natural and cultural resources of Texas and to provide hunting, fishing and outdoor recreation opportunities for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

 

HIRING CONTACT: Justin Fleury, (512) 389-4367, Email: justin.fleury@tpwd.texas.gov

PHYSICAL WORK ADDRESS:4200 Smith School Road, Austin, TX 78744

 

GENERAL DESCRIPTION: 

Under the direction of the State Park Division's Planning and Geospatial Resources Director, this position is responsible for geographic information system (GIS) work involving project delivery, ranging from geodatabase design and management to the development of specialized mapping applications that meet Division-wide business needs.  This position is responsible for creating, editing, and maintaining geospatial data related to the division's Facility Asset Management System (FAMS), the Park Business System (PBS), and Natural and Cultural Resource databases.  Duties require specialized knowledge and skills in GIS database management using ESRI software and technology. Responsible for developing and maintaining comprehensive documentation for stakeholder training and team development, including the processes, protocols, and structure of GIS applications, data services, and geodatabases.  Works as part of a GIS team to support initiatives across division as directed by the Planning and Geospatial Resources Director. Performs additional duties as assigned.  Complies with all Agency, Division and Branch rules, regulations and procedures.  

 

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Education:

GIS Analyst II and GIS Analyst III:

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor's degree or higher with coursework in GIS or Computer.

Experience:

GIS Analyst II:

6 months of professional experience in creating, editing, and/or managing spatial data and/or table structures;

Demonstrated experience providing GIS support for a Facility Asset Management System (or similar software) such as OpenGov, Cartegraph or comparable platforms;

Demonstrated experience providing GIS support for a Park Business Management System (or similar software) such as Aspria or comparable platforms.

GIS Analyst III:

Two years of professional experience in creating, editing, and/or managing spatial data and/or table structures;

One year of professional experience with geodatabase management and mapping application development using ESRI tools and techniques; or similar software.

Licensure:

Must possess or be able to obtain, within 30 days of employment, a valid class "C" Texas driver's license.

NOTE:  Retention of position contingent upon obtaining and maintaining required license.

 

ACCEPTABLE SUBSTITUTIONS: 

Education:

One additional year of the required experience in creating, editing and/or managing spatial date and/or table structures may substitute for 30 hours of the required education with a maximum substitution of 120 semester hours.

Experience:

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Master's degree may substitute for 6 months of the required experience in creating, editing and/or managing spatial data and/or table structures.

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Education:       

GIS Analyst II and III:

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor's degree in Geography, Natural Resources, Environmental Management, Computer Science, or closely related field with coursework in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) or Computer Science.

Experience:

GIS Analyst II:

One year of professional experience in creating, editing, and/or managing spatial data and/or table structures;

Six months of experience providing GIS support for a Facility Asset Management System (or similar software) such as OpenGov, Cartegraph or comparable platforms; 

Six months of experience providing GIS support for a Park Business Management System (or similar software) such as Aspria or comparable platforms.

NOTE:  Experience may have occurred concurrently.

GIS Analyst III:

Four years of professional experience in creating, editing, and/or managing spatial data and/or table structures;

Two years of professional experience with geodatabase management and mapping application development using ESRI tools and techniques; or similar software;

Demonstrated experience leading GIS projects in a multi-user environment;

Demonstrated experience with multiple programming languages or frameworks (ESRI APIs, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Python, or equivalent).

NOTE:  Experience may have occurred concurrently.

 

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

GIS Analyst II

Knowledge of GIS software, concepts, and techniques;

Knowledge of geodatabase design, development, and maintenance;

Knowledge of creating, editing, and managing table structures associated with geospatial data

GIS Analyst III: Knowledge of GIS Analyst II, PLUS;

Knowledge of field mapping and data collection techniques and technologies with ESRI software/mobile apps;

Knowledge in the establishment and management of data schemas, and the structure of geospatial data in a multi-user enterprise geodatabase;

Knowledge of database/geodatabase system integration including programming, software, hardware, security and networking needs;

Knowledge of computer programming languages or frameworks (ESRI APIs, Javascript, HTML/CSS, Python, or equivalent);

Knowledge of natural and cultural resource management concepts;

GIS Analyst II:

Skill in GIS project development, delivery and maintenance

Skill in planning and implementing project work tasks and workflows;

Skill in providing GIS support for Facility Asset Management Systems (or similar software) related to outdoor recreation. 

Skill in providing GIS support for Business Management Systems (or similar software) related to outdoor recreation

Skill in effective verbal and written communication;

GIS Analyst III: Skill of GIS Analyst II, PLUS;

Skill in complex GIS analysis, tools and techniques for resource, business and facility management.

Skill in managing multiple projects involving the design, testing, and implementation of GIS applications or other initiatives involving numerous stakeholders in multi-user environment;

Skill in developing procedural manuals and how-to documents for GIS tasks;

GIS Analyst II:

Ability to provide GIS technical assistance and guidance to variety of personnel in the agency;

Ability to integrate State Parks GIS data with other programs, databases and systems;

Ability to acquire new technical skills and programming methodologies and transfer them to other staff;

GIS Analyst III: Ability of GIS Analyst II, PLUS;

Ability to provide technical assistance and guidance in the development and design of complex multidivisional GIS projects including data collection, geodatabase and application development

Ability to integrate data from various sources and apply analytic and cartographic techniques to represent information appropriately;

Ability to work independently with little or no supervision.
